If depression doesn't exist, is that why I won't leave my house? Do you honestly think laziness is the reason I was reported as a missing person to the police? If depression doesn't exist, why do I cry when I glance at myself in the mirror. Why am I isolating myself from family and friends? Why did I cut into my wrists? Why did I abuse substances, if depression didn't exist? &#x200B; An open letter to all those people out there saying "just be happy". That's cute. Recently it's been on mind, as I'm hitting new lows, but I don't think I could ever do it cause I'm just so in love with my boyfriend. Though, if he ever betrayed me who knows what I'd do. I don't know myself. It feels like I have no one, except him, and I know what men are like after being cheated on before in past relationships.

When exactly does free will happen? [SEP] To begin with, obviously you are not in control of where you were born, the surrounding circumstances, your genetics and how your brain developed. You dont get to choose your family if you have one, how they treat you, where you grow up and what happened in your childhood. And yet we know that these things deeply influence your personality and maladaptive coping mechanisms, if not completely determine them. You continue to go out into the world, every option available to you at any time is relegated to circumstances outside of your control. And then you have your own irresistible impulses. Like for instance, maybe someone offends you, and you react in anger, you say mean things. I dont really see these reactions as a choice as much as I see them as irresistible impulses. When you cant control your emotions and reactions to things, how much free will can you have? And even when you have learned to cope better and not react in anger so much, you are still propelled by an impulse to achieve something based on what you *want*, and I think that what we want is really not something can be helped, ever. The most clear example is sexual orientation. You desire what you desire, theres really no way of changing that. And it even goes as far as your own thoughts. You think you are making them happen. But any meditator will tell you that you cant really stop your thoughts, they happen without you. Theyre really kind of holding you hostage. Really, try to stop thinking for a minute. Youll find that you probably cant. So we are relentlessly determined by these processes that we feel like we are making happen, and yet we cant help them. We could get further into it and say that once you become a skilled meditator, you dont have to believe or give in to your thoughts all the time. But even the impulse to become a meditator came from some mixture of environmental circumstances and predisposition. Mainly I am wondering what you think about these irresistible impulses. I mean, do you think that any action you take can ever really be removed from your desires, the irresistible and even biological urges that rule your mind?

An encounter in the parking lot. [SEP] Staying at a business hotel in Mito. Its past 10 PM. I step outside for one last smoke before bed. Theres an ashtray tucked away in a dim passagewaya narrow link between the small, recessed entrance and the main parking lot. The midwinter night air is biting, but it feels just right against my skin, still flushed from the bath. I step slightly into the lot and light a cigarette. Out of nowhere, a white-and-grey calico cat emerges silently under the glare of an LED spotlight. In that beam, its white fur glows with a strange, vivid brilliance. I click my tongue to let it know Im there. The cat gives me a fleeting glancea silent acknowledgmentand disappears toward the back of the lot. I look up. A massive "Super Hotel" sign clings to the side of the building. Yellow background, white lettering, glowing defiantly against the void of the night sky. Suddenly, the same cat streaks past my feet. It shows no sign of wariness, yet it isn't friendly, either. It simply moves away, following some invisible map. It leaps onto a fence as if navigating its usual route and presses its nose against a power line that stretches diagonally across the wall. Sniff, sniff. Its tail is thick. I click my tongue once more to call out. The cat has a sharp, intense face; its coat is remarkably clean. Soon losing interest in the wire, it returns to its routine and vanishes into the dark. He had his freedom. But he had no way to escape the cold. Pitiable, yet somehow untouched by it. In that moment, something about freedom stayed with me.

Special Needs Parent Burned Out and Having an Existential Crisis [SEP] I'm the mother of a 9 year old boy with high functioning autism, ADHD and most probably Oppositional Defiance Disorder. He is sweet, but he has the most spectacular temper and can get violent. I'm worn out by the daily struggles and the constant worrying about his future. I've tapped out all the help I can get and compared to most people, I am blessed to be able to be a stay-at-home mom, but I never saw myself as a stay-at-home type. I have 2 degrees from university and I tried to have a career, but I went through 2 bouts of diagnosed depression due to the stress of raising my son and I couldn't balance taking care him, my career and myself so one had to go. Don't get me wrong, I love my son more than life itself and even in my darkest mental states, I went on living for him. Even with therapy, meditation, staying fit, giving up drugs and alcohol when my use became problematic, I still feel STUCK. I wanted to do so much more with my life than what I had and I'm just feeling like life has made a joke of all my efforts and the "promise" those around me kept saying I had. Instead I'm poised to become a failure as a mom because my son will probably not have much of a future due to his difficulties. I'm trying to take it day by day and do the best I can, but all of my effort just feels useless and I'm wondering what the point of existence is if I spend my entire life stuck. There are people who would've been more nurturing and patient with a boy with needs like my son, who actually wanted to be a stay-at-home parent, so why me? How do I find purpose for what I gave up and the constant effort I expend that never seems good enough?

Why do you believe in Free Will? [SEP] I am here, not to argue for determinism, but rather to address the absolutely obvious question: Why would there be any such thing as free will? Determinists have given numerous arguments for their views, yet believers in free will simply talk about how depressing it is, and how they "feel like we have free will". The existence of free will is, in my opinion, an absolutely twisted pseudoscientific idea derived from religion and pride, not any scientific or logical bases. Now, I understand fully that nothing can be proven...but I am quite interested in the issue of determinism and derive pleasure from arguing about its logic. While the belief in free will, just as that of religion, makes people happy in a depressing universe (not intrinsically so, but because of human biology), I can take no solace in a fact because I rightly know that both religion and free will were made up by humans, to explain existence and to cope with existential questioning. Simply give me an argument for the logical thought-process that you go through, and how this leads you to the conclusion of the existence of free will.

I just overcame a 4-month existential crisis [SEP] This post is for you if you are currently dealing with existential dread. I really wish I would have read this somewhere when I was suffering through it recently. I am 31 years old in my life has recently changed completely. I went from owning a debt collection agency in New York to being a software engineer in California, I left a six year long relationship, I sold my house and business, I sold my car, and I got back in shape after letting myself go. All of this sounds very positive but it was a huge shock to my system. I feel like I had a midlife crisis at 30 because the reality that time keeps moving forward bringing me closer to death finally set in. I realized that I wasted my 20s in a bad relationship, and I am roughly 10 years clean from a bad heroin addiction. I couldn't help but feel like I've wasted my entire adult life even if I'm on the right track now, I should be further ahead in life. Of course you can argue that I'm doing well for myself but the feeling of not living up to my own expectations, and the fear of never finding a wife or starting a family was terrifying, it is still terrifying. I got to a point where the only thing I was ever thinking about was my own mortality, the actual fact that I was actually going to die someday, and confronting my lack of spirituality. My mother is a very religious person and my father died when I was a teenager. I never got to talk to my father about these things, and my mother is so confident in an eternal afterlife that I envy her but I can't believe the same thing. I had talked about this with a therapist that I really trust and respect. The best that he could tell me is that the universe existed for billions of years without me and everything was just fine, and that everyone is going to die so it's the most natural thing in the world. None of that made me feel any better because as insignificant as my life might be to the universe, my life is the most significant thing ever to me. So relatively speaking, there's no solace there. I've never had suicidal ideations and I'm not going to say that this existential crisis caused me to feel that, because that would be counterintuitive. But I think I can finally understand the mindset that a suicidal person might experience because my very existence was torturous for about 4 months. I would talk to everyone I knew to try to figure out how other people cope with this but I realize that the majority of people just don't fixate on this. I think that your own mortality is just a vague concept that people think that they've accepted but in reality, very few people need to wrestle with that reality when they are young. The good news that I wanted to share with everyone is that it's gone. The existential dread, the never-ending impending sense of Doom and terror that I lived with for 4 months straight finally let go of me. I'm still distressed by the same thoughts but I'm not so fixated on it that I can't function or find happiness. I moved to a city where psilocybin mushrooms were decriminalized and even sold over the counter in dispensaries. I hadn't tripped on mushrooms since I was 18 but I had a gut feeling that it's what I needed to fix this. Don't get discouraged if that's not something that you are up for because I do genuinely believe now that the obsession would have passed with time, it may have taken a little bit more time but I've been skateboarding and I think that has been extremely healthy for me both physically and mentally. I would encourage anyone who is struggling with existential dread to pick up something you're passionate about as a kid because when you are a kid you pursue things for pure happiness instead of money. For what it's worth, one relatively low dose mushroom trip was enough to turn the volume on those intrusive thoughts down significantly. It gave me a sense of spirituality and a sense of being part of something greater than myself. I think I'm going to make a point to do it roughly once every year as a form of maintenance. Just now that if you are struggling with existential dread, it feels like there is no end in sight but having just escaped from it, I want to share a little bit of Hope with everyone. Hang in there. It will be okay.

Loneliness has its roots in words, in an internal conversation that nobody answers; solitude has its roots in the great silence of eternity. - Kent Nerburn

I'm (23f) glad I didn't take my life at fifteen. [SEP] *Thank you to the people who gave me a shiver and gold award. And thank you to the people who gave me encouraging/positive words in the comments.* Since I was a child I had depression (I have other mental illness and health conditions as well) but wasn't diagnosed officially with it until I hit 18. My depression slowly got worse over the years. Started being suicidal in 10th grade. One day at the age of fifteen i wrote my suicide letter went into my parents room grab the handgun and pointed to my head with my eyes closed. I remember I had my finger on the trigger thinking "I'm sorry mom and dad, please don't blame yourself for what I'm about to do I love you." As I was getting ready to pull the trigger the energy of their room change. It felt like I wasn't alone i felt someone put their hand on my shoulder and squeeze. After that it trigger a flash back of memories of the people I love. I tried opening my eyes but I couldn't my memories were playing like a silent film. When my senses came back i put the gun down and destroyed my suicide letter. Went into my room and cried for hours because I felt like I was selfish. I vowel that day to never attempt suicide again even if I'm suicidal. Im 23 now and even though I still deal with depression and my other illnesses I'm grateful I didn't end my life that day. Life hasn't been all rainbows though the years. I had failures after failures. I also had small victories but sadly only focus on the failures. but for the last three months of this year I learn so much about myself. I learned to forgive myself for my failures. I learn my failures were a detour so I could learn the lessons that I needed. Im becoming more self aware everyday. I admitting to the problems i have to myself and others that I wasn't ready to face but it needed to be said. For the first time it finally feels like I'm healing. And finally for the first time(in a very long time) I feel hopeful.

You Dont Fear Death. You Fear Running Out of Time. [SEP] # Death is nothing to us.  Epicurus Yet here you are, terrifiednot of being dead, but of never having lived. You tell yourself you fear the unknown, the void, the loss of consciousness. But the truth? You dont fear death. You fear **dying before you ever truly became who you should have been**. This isnt just your fearits the **human condition laid bare**. And those who came before you knew it well. But heres where I differ. They wrote about it. I have lived it. # I Have Stared Into the AbyssAnd It Stared Back. I have felt the weight of existence press against me, not as an abstract concept, not as an intellectual exercise, but as something that wrapped around my bones and whispered: **You are running out of time**. I have ruminated endlessly on free will, reality, and the nature of meaning itselfnot because it was a fun debate, but because it clawed at me in the quiet hours when no distractions could save me. I have watched people avoid this truth, **turning away from their own mortality with triviality and noise.** And I have seen how that avoidance poisons themhow it makes them weak, how it kills them long before their bodies do. I refuse to live that way. # Youve Been Given the Gift of Existential FreedomAnd Youre Wasting It. # Life is not a problem to be solved, but a reality to be experienced.  Kierkegaard So why do you treat existence like an equation, a puzzle, an obstacle? Why do you run from the weight of being alive, distracting yourself with petty comforts? Kierkegaard warned of **living in despair without even realizing it**the sickness of never becoming your true self. Ask yourself: **If you died today, would you die as yourself? Or just as the mask you wore to avoid that question?** I used to wear that mask. Then I ripped it off. I realized that if I was going to be alive, truly alive, I had to take responsibility for my own existence. **No one was going to hand me meaningI had to make it.** # Youre So Afraid of Death That Youve Forgotten How to Live. # Being-toward-death is the condition for authentic existence.  Heidegger Heidegger knew: **Most people dont livethey exist in avoidance, pushing thoughts of death aside, letting themselves be absorbed in triviality.** You **live like you have time**, but the truth is: **You dont.** Every moment wasted is a moment you will never get back. I have felt this truth at my core. I have wrestled with it, and I have burned because of it. It has made me angry. Not at deathbut at the people who waste their lives fearing it. **What have you done today that justifies your existence?** # Your Fear of Death is an Excuse to Stay Weak. # The only way to deal with an unfree world is to become so absolutely free that your very existence is an act of rebellion.  Camus You are **not afraid of death.** You are afraid of being **so free that you have no excuses left.** Ive learned that people **love** their excuses. They cling to them like life rafts, floating aimlessly, because the alternative is terrifying: **To stand on your own, to accept radical freedom, to realize that every wasted second is your own fault.** No gods to blame. No system to rage against. No cosmic injustice holding you down. Just **you, your choices, and the clock that never stops ticking.** I have chosen rebellion. Not against society, not against institutions, but against the **part of me that wanted to stay asleep.** What about you? # Your Time is Already Running Out. * Marcus Aurelius told you: **"You could leave life right now. Let that determine what you do and say and think."** * Seneca warned you: **"It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste much of it."** * Every philosopher who ever mattered has been screaming at you to **wake up.** And so am I. I have felt the full weight of this truth, and I am handing it to you now. The question is: **Youre running out of time. Whats stopping you from living as if that were true?** No justifications. No distractions. Just the question. **Sit with it.** And if something inside you resistsif you feel the impulse to scroll away, to avoid thisask yourself why. Some of you will **think** about this and ***move on***. Others will *feel* it ***linger***. If something in this resonates with you, Id like to hear your thoughts. No pressure, just an open space.

My therapist cried in a session and another therapist told me to quit her ASAP [SEP] I have been seeing my therapist for a few years but just started recently feeling comfortable enough to open up about my past trauma to her. Upon doing so, she cried. She did try to hold it back but eventually she cried then immediately apologized and told me that I remind her of her daughter and she cares about me. It honestly was the first time I've felt love from a parental figure. However, during that time I was actually having a mental breakdown. I was reliving my trauma everyday and it impacted my work greatly. My boss was not understanding and my physichiatrist eventually recommended a extensive therapy group with a "great therapist." This therapist was not at all what I expected. She was incredibly into the "tough love" approach. She made everyone go in a circle and talk about their most traumatic moments. I have social anxiety and these were strangers so I did not really participate in that. But I did talk about my therapy experience and my coping mechanisms and such. She eventually found out that my therapist cried once in a session. She told me that was "beyond unprofessional" and that I should "drop her immediately." I actually did end up dropping her only to get a horrible experience with another therapist. One recommended by the therapist that told me to drop my initial therapist. I was so sad and eventually went back to my initial therapist. I haven't seen anything wrong but I can't get help but feel insecure about my own decision. Am I making the right choice? Is it okay to go to someone cause they feel like a friend you can open up to? Are emotions bad and unprofessional for a therapist to express? *LIL' UPDATE* Wow! Thank you all so much for the comments and awards. It was so nice to read all of your experiences, I'm so overwhelmed with happiness rn to not feel so alone! I have seen 8 therapists in my life and I have never felt this comfortable with one. It honestly was the first time I haven't regretted telling a professional my personal trauma. Although not everyone agrees with this approach, her emotion ultimately showed me that I have people that care about me and it really helped me in a time when I really just needed compassion. With that being said, I am continuing to see my empathetic therapist as that is what works best for me. Thank you again for all of your reassurance and encouragement in helping me choose what's best for me. I struggle a lot with decision making so I was really in my head about this. Anywho, just wanted to say you are part of a wonderful community here and I hope you all find happiness/peace. I'm not there quite yet, but baby steps are okay.

My take [SEP] There is no objective meaning of life. Whatever meaning we as a society or an individual have given it is completely random although it maybe doesn't feel like it at first, or at second thought. Considering the fact that people go into solitary retreats for years to ruminate on life's meaning, it will take hard work and time to realize this. From personal experience I can tell you it is the most difficult thing you'll ever undertake as it involves rigourous self analysis, and the most rewarding. Good, bad, happiness, sadness, are all our own creations and labels . Happiness is basically this: Feeling you have when you get 'what' you want. That's it, nothing more. The 'What' written above is where the whole secret lies. Have you ever asked yourself why you want what you want? We think that we have our reasons , but the reality of these reasons is that they are just subjective concepts created by humanity through various structures and institutions like society, religion, family, relationships, morality, success etc. We have deluded ourselves into thinking that we have reasons for the way we live life, but actually we don't have any. This is because objective reasons don't exist, in fact reason itself is our own creation or label. Think about it, imagine earth without humanity, where is the reason coming from?do you really think you have instincts? have you ever really tried to control your 'instincts' ?are we copying other animals? some eat their own children so why don't we start doing that? what is the basis of your deciding what is right or wrong? Is any kind of pain really an objective negative experience or just a reaction to attachment? Think!!..a lot!..don't jump to conclusions.. "The greatest enemy of knowledge is not ignorance, it is the illusion of knowledge" Consider this: (read it like a self reflection or conversation with someone) I like dressing up and looking good--why? because I like looking attractive-- why? because people treat you better in fact some even get in awe of me literally, good things just seem to come easier, who doesn't want to be good looking?? -- why do you want good things easier? because it makes my life easier-- why do you want that? because an easier life makes me happier, who the hell wouldn't want that!!=( did you notice how 'reason' morphed into 'happiness' ?) Now that maybe is the thinking of many of you. Maybe some of you think its true for everyone. But that actually is not the case as some people do things knowing that it would make their lives tougher, just because they wanna do that. This is what it comes down to: I want A because it makes me happy. I want B because it makes me happy. I want C because it makes me happy and so on. People think its A, B, or C that is making them happy but that's an illusion. Think, if A made you happy, then A would make anyone happy, but there isn't a single thing in life that everyone wants, including life itself. That means your "happiness" has something to do with you as a person, with your 'want'. Here's where 'motivation theory of pleasure' comes in (Google it). This theory basically states that whether something is ' desirable' or not is something that you decide in your mind based on whatever, which means that A,B and C dont have any real relation to your happiness, they are just actors or imposters in your life story. In other words, something makes you happy because you think it makes you happy, that's it. Its kind of a self fulfilling prophecy. In reality, you actually want nothing. Desire or happiness is your own creation, and so is sadness and suffering. And finally, you yourself are your own imagination, or belief. You don't really exist , you just think you do. In fact what you call thought or mind or memory is your own creation. To put it crudely, life is essentially an illusion itself. You are not much different from a rock lying by the side of road. Think for yourself! dont take my word for it. Few people you can check out: Carlo Michelstaedter Mitchell Heisman Gustave Flaubert Michel Foucault You can also read philosophies like budhism, advaita Hinduism, taoism, stoicism. And ya as far as science is concerned, it will never answer 'why' of life, only 'how'. It will tell you proton and electron attract each other but not why they do that. Science by its very nature is only concerned with 'how'. There will always be some particle which has some properties. Also read about ' politicization of science' while you're at it.

When you die your life starts over again from the beginning [SEP] Time has essentially been proven to be non-liner. We live in a deterministic block universe. The only differences between past, present, and future are within the constructs of your mind. There is no such thing as now as every point in time is equally real. As such, youre simply a time-slice which exists eternally and is experiencing a subjective flow of time. Once your conscious is terminated your perception of reality starts from the beginning. The same life youve already lived plays out again. There was never a time when you didnt exist and theyll never be a time when you cease to exist, youre just exist eternally trapped within your own slice of space-time. I believe this is the only fully coherent view on the nature of existence. The idea that you didnt exist before you were born and will cease to exist doesnt make sense. If you only exist for finite amount of time and dont exist for an infinite amount of time the odds of you existing right now are zero. This model of existence also solves the hard problem of consciousness as it makes conscious experience inherent to the universe in a way that simply slides in with the rest of what we know about space-time without coming up with stuff like that chair over there has a certain level of consciousness. If there are any good counter agreements to this claim Id love to here them, but I think this is the strongest model on the nature of existence and Ive yet to hear anything else more sensible.

How I got out of my existential crisis a year ago. [SEP] I was talking to a friend today about the existential crisis that I had last year. It was one of the most, of the the most challenging experience that I have ever faced. There was, however, a very, very happy ending. I figured it would give some hope to the people here. Three years ago, after many many things going wrong in my life, internally and externally, I was having insane levels of stress. After months of that, I started experiencing derealization. For you guys that are not aware, derealization is a defense mechanism that our mind uses when we are passing through a lot of negative emotion. It turns off the prt of the brain that makes you accept life as how it is and be "inserte" in it,making you realize how absurd reality is. Since I was in a very, very introspective and desperate state, this realization did not help me. I began by questioning who, or, in that case what I was. Was I anything? Who am I to determine if I am anything at all? Does anything exist? As most of you guys know, it becomes almost impossible to live when you "know" that life is a fraud. I started missing being worried about "planet earth" things. Thankfully, my therapist was a anthropologist with a big philosophy background. He didn't want me to read philosophy or take me out of the crisis, instead, he said what I was going through, although painful, was something great that most people run from. He guided me through the whole questioning, making me find the cues myself. It was a great experience, I had the task to philosophize and come up with the answers that humans came up with thousands of years ago. Which "thought" got me out? I drew in my head two realities: the "real reality", which would be the truth: things have no meaning or quality. And the "human reality", which would be our body creating a lens that distorts the world and creates quality. This difference in "size"(the nothingness is a lot bigger than our life) bothered me. I, however, realized that difference was insignificant since it is our human minds that create this comparison. In the universe, nothing matters. I, after suffering a shit ton for months, had to kneel down to how things are and accept that life is just an experience. This acceptance triggered my recovery and turned me into a very, very optimistic person. I accepted my insignificance in an already insignificant world.

I may have Covid 19, my stoic view. [SEP] I have ticked all the check-boxes, I wear a mask (perhaps more than necessary) wash my hands, and stay isolated save my children, mother, girlfriend, and her son. I controlled what I could. However the past few days I have had a fever, though no coughing. It may just be a mild flu, too. No less I am getting tested tomorrow. Epictitus, and Marcus remind us over and over our bodies are not ours. They also remind us that life is short, and to keep death in mind because fortune can turn in a moment's notice. I sat on my couch last night, and used negative visualization to extrapolate the worst case. I have Covid, and I am going to die alone from it. This means that Thursday was the last time I hugged my children of 12 and 7, my house, career, car, all of it is meaningless, but this is all out of my control now. Why die shamefully? Why show my kids that death is indignant, and that its "not fair?" I got 40 years! I have a strong body, have made good use of it, have touch peoples lives, and have two good kids who enjoy being with their father and learning stoic principles. If worse comes to be, which is unlikely, I am thankful for my life and what I made if it, especially when I started down the path of stoicism several years ago. Many people live lives where they cannot say they even get several good years. I have already accepted death a few years ago and it has made my life much richer. It keeps first things first, and I have come to value things that do not cost any money. My anxiety and stress is little, and cherishing each moment makes live very long. It also allows me not to suffer in advance, since that is suffering in excess. It is the reason I am sitting here with a pounding headache typing this, but smile at the birds dancing about my bird-feeder, while I enjoy the quietude of an early summer morning. Anyway, Via face time, zoom, or whatever platform I will see my children if worse came to be, I will be cheerful, loving, and supportive to the very end. There is no other way to be! I have a job to do until my very last breath and will do it, this is what we are taught, this is why we practice. Thank you for reading, I feel its important for us to really practice our Stoicism, and this is going to be such a wonderful test.

But we as we are now will one day cease to exist for all eternity, and all memory of us along with it. Same with all those we love. So appreciate the time you've been given and cherish your loved ones while you can. And do all you can to get the most enjoyment and happiness out of your time. Don't waste away being miserable doing things you hate all your life. There is no purpose or meaning to life other than to enjoy it. Do what makes you and the ones you care about happy, fuck everything else.
